best_for: Groups who want an encrypted team chat they can host on their own server, and Matrix users who want a desktop client next to the browser and phone apps.
description:
Element is a messaging app from Element, a European company headquartered in the UK with offices across Europe and North America. It is led by the team that created Matrix, the open chat standard Matthew Hodgson and Amandine Le Pape started in 2014. Matrix itself is governed by the non-profit Matrix.org Foundation.

Chat one to one or in groups, and make voice and video calls from the same app. Organizations can run it on air-gapped networks with no internet link, or over low-bandwidth links such as mesh and satellite. Element pitches it as a self-hosted alternative to Microsoft Teams, and as a work replacement for WhatsApp or Signal.

points.title: Chat on an open network
points.text: Element is an end-to-end encrypted messenger built on Matrix, an open, decentralized network. You can join rooms on other Matrix servers, and an organization can run its own server instead of trusting someone else's.

points.title: Free for personal use and small setups
points.text: The apps are free and open source under the AGPL or GPL version 3. The free Community server suite covers non-professional use and trials for 1 to 100 users. Enterprise is priced per seat per month from 100 users, and Element does not publish those prices.

points.title: The browser can stand in
points.text: app.element.io runs the same client in a browser with nothing to install, which helps on a locked-down work PC. The desktop app adds its own window and notifications.

points.title: Windows installs per user
points.text: The Windows installer sets Element up for the current user only, so it needs no administrator rights. It comes in x64 and Arm64 builds, and the Windows listing keeps 169 versions.

points.title: On Linux, the .deb is the official route
points.text: Element runs its own apt repository for Debian and Ubuntu on x86_64 and aarch64. The Flathub package is listed by Element as community-maintained, and Flathub does not mark it as verified. Linux and macOS list only the current release here.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 13
points.text: The Mac build is one universal app for Intel and Apple silicon and needs macOS 13 or later. Element also offers nightly builds for testers on every desktop platform.
